title: Constant-rank determinant description of the smooth diagonal dualizing object
statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]), and let f:X\to S be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and smooth of relative dimension d\geq0 [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put P=X\times_S X with diagonal \Delta:X\to P [def-pc-base-change]. Choose derived categories for X and P, possibly in different universes [def-pc-derived-category]. Let h_\Delta witness preservation of quasi-coherent cohomology by the recorded R\Delta_* [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and let c:D_{QCoh}(P)\to D_{QCoh}(X) be a specified right adjoint of its full-subcategory restriction using h_\Delta. Let O_P be a quasi-coherent derived object with underlying object isomorphic to \mathcal O_P[0]. Write M=\Omega^1_{X/S} [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and M^\vee=\mathcal Hom(M,\mathcal O_X) [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Then there is an isomorphism c(O_P)\cong (\bigwedge^d M^\vee)[-d] in D(X), with the sheafified exterior power [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power].

proof.text: Properness makes the diagonal closed. X and P are Noetherian by finite type and base change. The smooth diagonal theorem gives Koszul-regular local generators; restrict its affine open neighbourhoods near each diagonal point to give the regularity witness in the Koszul duality theorem.

Identify the conormal with relative differentials. The latter is finite locally free of rank d. Stalks therefore have finrank d, so the constant locally constant function d satisfies the rank witness in Koszul duality. Apply that theorem with c and the literal single structure object, transporting O_P along its specified isomorphism.

Dualize the conormal isomorphism by precomposition and take its sheafified exterior power. For constant rank d, the rank-d stratum is all of X and the other strata are empty. Their extension-by-zero terms are zero, so the locally ranked exterior complex is isomorphic to the single exterior sheaf in degree d. Its derived image is the degree-zero single shifted by -d. Compose with the inverse Koszul-duality isomorphism. This also works for empty X and d=0.
